# ISSUE-38 — Verify and release Phase 2

The merged Chapter 2, **The Deferred Line**, is the release candidate. Extend the existing Playwright finale matrix to prove the full player journey and v1 upgrade, then use the same UI to check accessibility and the Pages build. Collect release evidence against the final candidate and leave production verification to the coordinator and maintainer after merge.

The WorkUnit sets size to `multi_area` and the approved profile to `detailed`. Allow about 12–18 hours for planning, implementation, review, and claim-bound validation, including time for a small defect fix and a CI rerun. The approved budget is 32 hours across an initial 8-hour lease and up to three explicit renewals. Pages deployment and maintainer sign-off follow merge. The agent plan-review gate and protected paths apply throughout. [WorkUnit](WORKUNIT.md)

## What we know

- `tests/e2e/journey.spec.ts:4` plays through Episode 000 to the map under both motion preferences. `tests/e2e/episode.spec.ts:19` checks the clean Episode 000 gates, designation, and reload. `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts:558` plays the four header/custody and Hunter/Trader combinations through Chapter 2, with each case currently seeding a rewritten copy of the completed v1 save before opening.
- `tests/fixtures/episode-000-complete-v1.json:2` contains the original schema shape, completed Episode 000, optional service and FORGE flags, preferences, and designation `OBS-02FF`. `src/progress/save.ts:168` lifts v1 global progress into v2 and initializes BBS and door state. `openSaveSession` writes the migrated save on opening at `src/progress/save.ts:221`. `tests/unit/save.test.ts:98` already checks the fixture and migration.
- The hub offers CONNECT when the endpoint's requirements hold and loads the BBS dynamically at `src/main.ts:119`. The Episode 000 ending shows the assigned designation at `src/main.ts:184`. Chapter 2 completion requires the episode, restoration, the signed manifest and the replay receipt read at `content/episodes/episode-002.json:5`. BBS completion writes progress before switching scenes at `src/bbs/progress.ts:94` and `src/main.ts:152`. The routing entry is a follow-up in Messages, and the existing finale asserts its read state and the audit after reload at `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts:829`.
- The two declarative doors are Relay Trivia and The Forgotten Archive (`content/doors/`); the two code doors are Signal Hunter and Relay Trader (`src/doors/code-doors.ts:6`). `src/doors/registry.ts:21` builds declarative doors from bundled data, and `src/doors/code-doors.ts:19` and `:36` lazily import the code doors. `src/content/browser-split.ts:33` includes the declarative doors, BBS records, events and signed repair data in the BBS payload. `scripts/content-plugin.ts:22` validates all authored content and emits the production payloads and manifest.
- Keyboard navigation already exercises each door in individual tests (`tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts:47`, `:327`, `:845`, `:922`). The finale's keyboard branch still clicks the map and routing entry and programmatically focuses the prompt at `:786–802`. `tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts:64` disables WebGL through the canvas API while preserving 2D, but only plays to the hub. The existing Chapter 2 matrix tests system and explicit reduced motion at `:558–598` and synchronous ending text at `:758–766`. BBS viewport coverage remains open. The stylesheet intentionally scrolls the log and menu at `src/style.css:181` and `:267–287`.
- `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts:18` serves `dist/` under `/signal-lost/` by interception and bypasses interception in live mode. `tests/e2e/startup.spec.ts:9` checks startup deferral. The finale currently checks assets for its selected code door and performs its last network assertion before its final reload (`tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts:600`, `:823–842`). `tests/e2e/budget.spec.ts:13` caps gzip size at 60 KiB for the entry and 170 KiB for the environment, and `:19` requires 20 renders over two seconds on software WebGL.
- `Browser tests` runs the full Playwright suite on PRs and main using Ubuntu and Chromium (`.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:3–25`). `playwright.config.ts:10–16` and `tests/e2e/global-setup.ts:3` supply the production build, Pages URL and Chromium launch options. `Deploy to GitHub Pages` builds and publishes `dist/` on main (`.github/workflows/pages.yml:3–6`, `:28–45`). The planner and tester use the isolated Linux native Codex path in `.swarm/config.yaml:16–18` and `:63–67` for source/static work.

## What we're assuming

- The supplied tree is the approved merged Chapter 2 snapshot. The shipped content and tests are present, but the sandbox has no Git checkout metadata. The coordinator should record the approved base, candidate tree and final merge SHA from its trusted checkout.
- The existing four finale rows can absorb the release checks in place. Confirm Playwright discovery and use the first candidate CI run to check duration against the current 120-second test timeout and 30-minute job timeout. Use state-based waits and the existing staged-ending clock check if needed in its existing animated coverage. Keep the timeouts and frame/bundle ceilings.
- A version bump is allowed when required for this release. The available contract gives no target package version. Keep the current package version unless the release owner supplies one, then update `package.json` and the two root version fields in `package-lock.json` together. The existing v1-to-v2 save schema is independent of the package version.

## Open questions

- The snapshot identifies the Phase 2 parent as [Epic #23](https://github.com/supernovae/signal-lost/issues/23) (`.swarm/active/workunit.json:4`). Its definition-of-done text is unavailable in the supplied files. The coordinator retrieves the parent body from GitHub and reconciles its exact checklist against the PR template in `TEST_PLAN.md` before PR publication. Local implementation can proceed with the seven approved criteria.
- The sandbox cannot resolve or build `e54cde0` without Git history, or measure Chromium or the deployed site. The coordinator verifies the baseline identity and runs the two-build comparison in a trusted Linux Git checkout. CI demonstrates browser and frame evidence. The coordinator verifies the merged Pages deployment and runs the live journey. The maintainer records hand play. The focused commands and evidence locations are in `TEST_PLAN.md`.
- Firefox, Safari, real GPU performance and mobile layouts have no release evidence in this WorkUnit. The shipped browser harness targets Chromium and the acceptance viewport is 1280×720.

## Implementation

1. **Extend the finale matrix in `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts`.** Replace the header/Trader pointer row with **Chapter 2 release journey from a clean save** and the header/Hunter keyboard row with **Chapter 2 release journey from the version 1 fixture**. Keep the custody/Hunter pointer row with system reduced motion and the custody/Trader keyboard row with animation, and keep the existing rejection, gating, optional practice/market and attribution checks.
   - For the clean case start in Playwright's empty context. Register the page-error listener before navigation. At the opening, check persisted progress is empty by read-only observation after app boot and verify CONNECT is unavailable when first joining. Use `completeEpisode` from `tests/e2e/helpers.ts:18` through the Analyzer, Decoder, and Inquiry. Wait for the Episode 000 ending and capture the generated designation from the ending UI, then use CONTINUE. Reload, rejoin, and confirm the same designation and earned CONNECT. Leave optional FORGE unopened. Use the normal animated ending, await the audit with a bounded assertion, and activate CONTINUE normally.
   - For the v1 case use `seedSaveOnce(page, completedV1)` with the file's exact text before initial navigation. Check that the app writes v2, preserves Episode 000's recorded facts, `OBS-02FF`, and the fixture's audio, motion and effects preferences, with no reset notice and no Chapter 2 completion yet. Use the migrated designation at sign-in. Have this case earn the manifest through Hunter first. Its visits to the other doors are described below.
   - Reuse the finale's visible route through the Forgotten Board, Q17 and its evidence, `SUBMIT DEFERRED`, the Archive training shelf, the recovery console, and the Annex. Assert the proof and learned order before they enable the next step, the restoration result and MAINTAINER, the verified manifest, and the Annex comparison and reconstruction results. Put a second clean reload after SPOOL-02 is restored and before manifest acquisition. Rejoin with the earned identity and verify the restored directory, Annex and manifest-door access before proceeding. Keep the final reload on both named journeys. Check the Chapter 2 ending text and seal audit, CONTINUE, the newly published UNASSIGNED entry, and the retained audit and read status on re-entry after reload, with no replay of the ending. Assert `pageerror` after the last reload and checkpoint. Any save access after the v1 fixture's initial seed is observational.
2. **Exercise fallback, motion and input in the existing rows.**
   - Export a short `disableWebGl` helper from `tests/e2e/helpers.ts` by lifting the existing initialization script in `tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts:64`. Use it there and in the custody/Hunter row, before the first navigation, and forward ordinary context calls with their arguments intact. The custody/Hunter row retains a v1-derived setup, with `reducedMotion: null`, emulated `reduce`, and screen effects enabled so hidden interference tests reduced motion directly. Confirm `data-render=fallback` and the CSS fallback at opening and after reload. Play Chapter 2 through the real terminal and assert the ending, saved progress and usable terminal afterward. Retain the ordinary-render v1 case with system `no-preference` to independently verify the migrated explicit reduce setting. At BBS and ending checkpoints check motion is off and the interference is hidden. Both reduced-motion cases must render the final story and audit immediately on entry. Preserve the existing animated line-order and timer/disposal assertions in the custody/Trader row.
   - Use real `page.keyboard` events for all BBS, door, and follow-up interactions in the v1 keyboard journey. Reuse `typeCommand` and `activateBbsButton` in `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts:20–45` and use actual Tab/Shift+Tab, Enter or Space for controls outside the BBS menu. Replace or route around the shared finale's map and UNASSIGNED mouse actions and prompt focus shortcut using commands advertised by the shipped UI or keyboard traversal. Verify focus returns to the BBS prompt after each door exit, to CONTINUE at the ending, and to the OBS prompt when returning to the hub. Read a board message and complete Relay Trivia (answers 2 and 1) before the Chapter 2 gate. Learn the Archive order and verify the Hunter trace H3 on the main route. After Hunter has granted the manifest, play the Trader receipt transaction (claim, stamp, exchange) via the keyboard and verify its receipt and the same manifest with no duplicate reward. The clean route independently proves Trader can award the manifest.
   - Run that keyboard journey at 1280×720. Use a small local layout assertion in `bbs.spec.ts` on the signed-in main menu, a BBS reading or comparison screen, and an actionable screen in each of the four doors. Verify the log, Tools navigation and prompt have positive usable area inside the terminal and viewport and do not overlap. Check for horizontal overflow. Permit the log/menu's intentional vertical scrolling and verify the current output/action and representative focused control are readable/reachable inside their clipping containers. Record screen names in assertion failures. Use measured DOM boxes, focus and scrolling assertions with a small rounding tolerance.
3. **Complete Pages acceptance within the v1 keyboard journey.** Start recording HTTP(S) requests, failed requests, HTTP errors and page errors before the first navigation and check them after the final reload. Compare origin and path on request start so rejected or blocked requests on another origin still surface. Check success of production entry JS/CSS, the BBS connection, shared code-door content, both code-door chunks, and the contributor view on explicit opening. Include visible evidence from BBS records, both declarative door screens, and both code doors with the signed manifest. The production build validates the full authored inventory. Use the successful production payload requests and UI evidence together to check packaged content. Check lazy requests against the state before CONNECT and before each code door and credits opens. Reuse startup tests and the existing chunk matchers, using hashed names or index asset references. Do not require the browser to fetch individual authored JSON/JSONC files because Vite embeds those payloads. Keep the existing production interception fixture, Pages base, and protected workflow files. On an unexpected request, report event, URL, status or failure before diagnosing the source.
4. **Record size and reserve engine changes for reproduced defects.** Reuse the unchanged bundle and frame budget test in Browser tests. The coordinator builds the exact historical baseline and the exact candidate separately and captures the comparable bytes and delta by the method in `TEST_PLAN.md`. If the journeys expose a defect, record the failing assertions first and fix the smallest responsible touchpoint. Use `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts` or `src/terminal/terminal.ts` for a demonstrated focus issue, `src/style.css` for a demonstrated layout issue, or the responsible existing save, BBS or build seam for a reproduced defect. Preserve story facts and shipped gates. File a follow-up for a large fix and record the open failure in the PR evidence.
5. **Update the four release docs and prepare the PR body.** Adjust `README.md:5–11` and `:36–44` to describe Episode 000 plus Chapter 2, Deep Field, the optional side activity, and local save compatibility. Keep the opening playtime scoped to Episode 000 unless measured. Update `docs/architecture.md:31–76` to reflect the layered Pages assets, v1 migration, both door formats and the fact-backed transition into the shared ending. Update `docs/content-authoring.md:72–185` with shipped BBS checks, events, examples, code vs declarative door authoring, and validation/preview links. Preserve the worked transmission example and any links asserted in unit tests. In `docs/roadmap.md:3–24` make a shipped section for Episode 000 and the delivered BBS, door and Chapter 2 features, and retain “None of this exists yet” for future ideas. Keep the Silent Observatory and optional future ideas there. Apply the PR checklist in `TEST_PLAN.md` with CI, bundle, document, and Epic evidence. After merge the coordinator watches the Pages run for the exact merge SHA, runs the clean journey in live mode, and records that result and the maintainer's hand play with gameplay evidence before closing the Epic.

## HANDOFF

- **Primary edits** — `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts:558` `finaleJourneys` and its loop, plus `joinWithEnter`, `typeCommand`, and `activateBbsButton` at `:14–45` as needed. Add `disableWebGl` to `tests/e2e/helpers.ts`, alongside the existing `seedSaveOnce` at `:5` and `completeEpisode` at `:18`. `tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts:64` retains its focused fallback test using the helper. Release docs edits are listed in step 5. `TEST_PLAN.md` holds the copy-ready PR body and size comparison. No new implementation files or deletions are planned. The two role outputs were absent from the supplied base snapshot.
- **Source entry points for investigation** — `src/main.ts:27` storage, `:54` fallback renderer, `:119` hub CONNECT, `:152` BBS ending, `:184` Episode 000 designation. `src/progress/save.ts:152` `loadSave` and `:221` `openSaveSession`. `src/bbs/connection.ts:27` `createBbsConnection`, `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts:11` `createBbsScene`, `src/bbs/door-session.ts:15` `createBbsDoorSession`, `src/bbs/progress.ts:82` `createBbsProgress`, `src/app/ending.ts:5` `createEnding`, and `src/terminal/terminal.ts:40` `createTerminal`. Build paths are `scripts/content-plugin.ts:9` `contentPlugin`, `src/content/browser-split.ts:33` `projectBbsContent`, and `src/doors/code-doors.ts:6` `CODE_DOORS`.
- **Reuse** — `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts:18`, `playwright.config.ts:5`, `tests/e2e/global-setup.ts:3`, `tests/e2e/startup.spec.ts:9`, `tests/e2e/budget.spec.ts:13`, `tests/fixtures/episode-000-complete-v1.json:1`, and `tests/unit/save.test.ts:98`. Existing BBS keyboard commands and role/title selectors have shipped counterparts, the raw v1 fixture has no Chapter 2 progress, and the protected CI job discovers the existing spec automatically. Checked against the source locations above.
- **Focused commands** — `npm exec --no -- prettier --check tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts tests/e2e/helpers.ts tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts README.md docs/architecture.md docs/content-authoring.md docs/roadmap.md`, `npm exec --no -- eslint tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts tests/e2e/helpers.ts tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts`, `npm exec --no -- tsc --noEmit`, `npm run test:e2e -- --list tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts`, and `npm test -- tests/unit/links.test.ts tests/unit/contribution.test.ts`. CI and coordinator commands and evidence ownership are detailed in `TEST_PLAN.md`.
- **Reopen the plan** if clean or migrated completion requires a new game feature, the fixture cannot migrate without a major compatibility rewrite, the Pages workflow would need a protected change, the trusted baseline cannot be verified, or a measured defect will exceed the claim budget. Keep blocked acceptance visible and have the coordinator resolve missing external evidence. A minor, reproducible defect remains in scope.
- **What this change breaks** — Repository search found the old finale titles in the generated test cases only. Keep the other two matrix cases and the earlier specs active, and use the new names in the PR/CI/live filters. `tests/e2e/journey.spec.ts` and `progress.spec.ts` rely on `completeEpisode` and `seedSaveOnce`; preserve those contracts. `tests/e2e/startup.spec.ts`, `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts`, `tests/unit/save.test.ts` and `tests/unit/episode.test.ts` reuse the canonical v1 fixture; preserve its bytes and original behaviors. `tests/unit/links.test.ts:8` and `tests/unit/contribution.test.ts:96` assert document links and the worked example; preserve those links/path/snippet, including the door-authoring guide. `README.md:34` and `CONTRIBUTING.md:24` link to these docs by path; keep paths unchanged. Keep the existing npm scripts, live switch, protected workflows, content solutions, and budget specs compatible.

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> Treat the merged Chapter 2 as the release candidate. Preserve protected workflow files and budget limits. Build the clean-save and real v1-save browser journeys using only shipped UI for progression. Close remaining no-WebGL, reduced-motion, keyboard, layout and Pages asset coverage. Keep maintainer live and hand-play tasks in the release checklist. Provide a ready-to-apply PR evidence checklist covering each Phase 2 Epic definition-of-done item. Do not claim live verification from the sandbox; the coordinator will watch production deployment and run the live journey after merge.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->

# ISSUE-38 test and release evidence

The acceptance numbers follow `WORKUNIT.md:26–32`. Until results are recorded, the cases below are planned checks. Attach the candidate source identity and actual result wherever evidence is reported.

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Case and pass evidence | Where it runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Clean Episode 000 → Chapter 2 journey | **Chapter 2 release journey from a clean save** starts with zero saved episodes/puzzles, joins and earns CONNECT and a designation via Episode 000 UI. It reloads after Episode 000 and after restoration, uses the same designation, earns its manifest via Trader, then verifies the actual ending, preserved-seal audit, UNASSIGNED and continuity after a final reload. The page-error list remains empty across all navigations. | CI, full `npm run test:e2e` in Browser tests. Post-merge live check below. |
| 2. Real v1 → Chapter 2 journey | **Chapter 2 release journey from the version 1 fixture** injects the original file bytes once, checks migrated schema 2, legacy Episode 000 facts, designation and preferences, and no reset or prior Chapter 2 completion. From there it proves the Hunter reward, completes the ending through the UI, and verifies audit and progress after reload. `tests/unit/save.test.ts:98` supplies focused migration diagnostics if relevant code changes. | CI, full browser run. Native Linux Codex for targeted save diagnostics. |
| 3. Keyboard, motion, fallback, layout | Named v1 journey uses keyboard-only BBS and door progression, including Relay Trivia completion, Archive training, Hunter verification, and Trader exchange. Verify focus at sign-in, door exits, ending and hub handoff. The v1 setting under an ordinary media preference and the custody/Hunter system-reduce case both show the complete ending synchronously, with motion off. The custody/Hunter row also denies WebGL before boot, asserts fallback before and after reload, and completes Chapter 2 via terminal actions. The v1 case runs at exactly 1280×720 and checks bounds and clipped/scrollable areas on the main menu, reading/COMPARE, and one usable screen per door. Existing animated, practices/market, and opening fallback cases still pass. | CI, full browser run on Chromium. |
| 4. Production assets and content | The v1 journey logs request starts, failed requests, and unsuccessful HTTP responses until the final re-entry. Every HTTP(S) request is on the Pages origin and within `/signal-lost/`. Assert entry JS and CSS, deferred BBS, shared code-door data, both code-door modules, and the contributor view on demand. Successful visible screen output proves BBS content and all four doors load. The startup cases continue to check eager-loading boundaries. | CI, same `dist/` and request interception for v1 and `startup.spec.ts`. |
| 5. Frame and bundle budget | Existing budget spec still requires at least 20 frames over two seconds on software WebGL, at most 60 KiB gzip for entry JS and at most 170 KiB gzip for environment JS. Record baseline, candidate and delta below, including byte total for JS/CSS, entry resources, environment and deferred growth. The comparison uses `e54cde0` even if current main has advanced. | CI for budget spec. Coordinator's trusted Linux checkout for the two builds and measurement. |
| 6. Docs and Epic evidence | Review the README for user-visible shipped scope, architecture for the build, BBS and save paths, authoring for current examples and validation, and roadmap for shipped vs future claims. Run focused link/example checks. Reconcile all Epic #23 definition-of-done rows against the canonical parent body and the prefilled PR checklist, with evidence and open state where needed. | Developer focused checks, independent tester review, coordinator's GitHub read and PR evidence review. |
| 7. Maintainer verification | After merge, record the Pages workflow URL and deployed merge SHA. Run the clean-save live command below, then record the maintainer's dated hand play through the ending, with route, browser/viewport, outcome and gameplay capture. Keep both sign-offs open through PR review and close the Epic only after both results are recorded and passing. | Coordinator's authorized live Linux Playwright/Chromium path and maintainer's desktop browser. |

## Developer — focused checks

Use the prepared Node 24 dependencies. In the isolated native Codex/Linux role, run the following with output captured to per-command logs in the role evidence area, including exit status and source identity. `--list` collects specs without launching Chromium or building the site.

```bash
npm exec --no -- prettier --check tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts tests/e2e/helpers.ts tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts README.md docs/architecture.md docs/content-authoring.md docs/roadmap.md
npm exec --no -- eslint tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts tests/e2e/helpers.ts tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts
npm exec --no -- tsc --noEmit
npm run test:e2e -- --list tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts
npm test -- tests/unit/links.test.ts tests/unit/contribution.test.ts
```

Check discovery for both named release cases and retained matrix cases. For a fix exposed by the journeys, add the smallest failing assertion to an existing test and rerun the affected diagnostic. Examples of exact targeted commands for applicable changes follow.

```bash
npm test -- tests/unit/save.test.ts tests/unit/episode.test.ts
npm test -- tests/unit/bbs.test.ts tests/unit/doors.test.ts tests/unit/adventure.test.ts tests/unit/events.test.ts
npm test -- tests/unit/render.test.ts tests/unit/scenes.test.ts
npm test -- tests/unit/pages.test.ts
npm run content:validate
```

Use the first set for a save/episode fix, the second for BBS/door/event logic, the third for render/scene logic, the fourth for build routing, and the last for changed authored content or its validator. For any additional touched files, include them in the focused formatter and applicable static checks. Keep logs as advisory developer evidence. Browser CI provides executable browser results.

## Tester — independent review and reuse

- Trace the two named cases to the first navigation, the only permitted initial v1 seed and the final reload. Confirm every intervening transition uses shipped UI, and that clean storage assertions observe, rather than establish, progress. Check actual Tab/Shift+Tab reachability, focus restoration, and all four door completions or equivalent door outcomes. Check that viewport assertions account for nested clipping and intended scrolling.
- Inspect motion setup order, fallback preservation of 2D, and the page-error and network listeners' lifetime. Confirm a response or resource is needed for every positive asset assertion and that an off-site request, same-origin wrong path, 404, missing chunk or page error fails the appropriate case. Trace the protected CI discovery path and compare the two tests' named checkpoints against criteria 1–4.
- Review changed docs against the shipped content and actual build pipeline, and inspect the evidence template against the approved criteria. Check that any discovered product defect has its regression case or a linked follow-up with an open status.
- Reuse developer logs and any applicable CI results for the same tree or unchanged relevant inputs. Record criterion-by-criterion review and outstanding checks in the tester validation artifact. Repeat only a targeted command for an observed failure, relevant input change, or specific unresolved coverage concern. Do not run the full trusted-base policy or browser in the role sandbox.

## CI and coordinator — run ownership

The existing `Browser tests` workflow installs Node 24.22.0 and Chromium, then runs `npm run test:e2e`. Global setup builds the production tree, and Playwright's fixture fulfills requests from `dist/`. No local HTTP server is required. For a targeted browser failure rerun in authorized Chromium, use `npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts tests/e2e/startup.spec.ts tests/e2e/budget.spec.ts`. The full pass on the final release candidate in the existing workflow is the PR browser evidence.

The coordinator runs the complete trusted-base policy in `.swarm/validation/required-checks.yaml:1–13` once after the roles finish and before publication. Scope and provenance of that run come from the approved claim. Developer and tester results are advisory. Use the trusted diff against the approved base to confirm protected paths and unapproved dependency or budget changes are absent.

| Check likely to exceed five minutes | Owner | Expected time | Evidence, applicability and reuse |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Full Browser tests workflow, including dependency/browser setup, `npm run test:e2e`, budget and all other specs | CI | 5–15 min normally, 30 min job cap | Link the successful Actions job and named cases. Record tested checkout SHA and candidate tree (including a PR merge checkout when relevant). Tester and coordinator reuse it for unchanged browser/build inputs. |
| Trusted-base required policy on final candidate | coordinator | 5–20 min across policy checks, individual timeouts per YAML | Reuse the claim-bound validation attestation and step logs with the approved policy and final tree identity. Publication reuses the attestation. |
| Two clean bundle builds and byte comparison below | coordinator | 5–15 min with dependencies available | Attach build logs and comparison to the PR. Record both full SHAs/trees, toolchain and base. Tester and maintainer reuse while build inputs match. |
| Watch `Deploy to GitHub Pages` through build and deploy for merge SHA | coordinator | 5–20 min after merge, plus queue | Link Actions run and Pages URL and record the deployed SHA. Epic closure reuses that result when linked to matching live evidence. |
| Live clean journey below, including clean dependency/browser setup if needed | coordinator | 5–10 min with setup | Attach console output or test result, time, published URL, deployment run and deployed SHA to the PR. Maintainer and Epic closure reuse it for that deployment. |
| Play the published chapter by hand and record gameplay | coordinator | 25–45 min including an Episode 000 lead-in when starting from a clean profile | Coordinator collects the maintainer's dated result, route, deployed SHA, browser/viewport, gameplay capture and issue links in the PR. Epic closure reuses it for that deployment. |

For local evidence record command, Node/browser versions where applicable, exit status, SHA or source snapshot identity, and whether there are uncommitted modifications. Trusted Git evidence can use `git rev-parse HEAD HEAD^{tree}` and `git status --short`. For a role snapshot without Git metadata, label the snapshot from the harness and provide the changed file digests or exact tested diff. Apply logs only when the relevant source, test, content, configuration and build inputs match.

## Coordinator — compare production size

Use an authorized Linux checkout with the historical Git object available. Confirm the baseline resolves to the expected SHA on main's history with `git rev-parse --verify 'e54cde0^{commit}'` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$baseline" origin/main`. Use separate clean detached worktrees to avoid stale assets or dependencies. Measure the candidate tree that CI and the required policy validate. Reuse a trusted candidate build if the same Node/npm versions, base, source and lockfile were used and its `dist/` is available. Record the toolchain, comparison command output and the production build logs. The historical size is a measurement, with the existing candidate limits checked by CI.

```bash
set -eu
baseline=$(git rev-parse --verify 'e54cde0^{commit}')
git merge-base --is-ancestor "$baseline" origin/main
candidate=$(git rev-parse --verify '<candidate-sha>^{commit}')
measure_dir=$(mktemp -d)
git worktree add --detach "$measure_dir/baseline" "$baseline"
git worktree add --detach "$measure_dir/candidate" "$candidate"
node --version
npm --version
for ref in baseline candidate; do
  (
    cd "$measure_dir/$ref"
    git rev-parse HEAD 'HEAD^{tree}'
    npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit --no-fund
    SIGNAL_LOST_BASE=/signal-lost/ npm run build
  ) >"$measure_dir/$ref.log" 2>&1
done
node --input-type=module - "$measure_dir/baseline/dist" "$measure_dir/candidate/dist" <<'NODE' >"$measure_dir/bundle-comparison.txt"
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, relative } from 'node:path';
import { gzipSync } from 'node:zlib';

const prefix = '/signal-lost/';
function readBuild(dist) {
  const files = readdirSync(dist, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true });
  const sizes = new Map();
  for (const file of files) {
```
